Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

School & learning

illustrate verb

put pictures in a book

also illustrated, illustrated book, illustrator, illustrations (in a book)

modern

M-O s.v. magazine, citing Egger: ephemeris … imāginibus ōrnāta

imāginibus ōrnāre

phrase: ōrnō, ōrnāre, ōrnāvī, ōrnātum with the ablative

to illustrate (with pictures)

A plain description in classical words: to furnish with pictures. The illustrator is a pictor.

Other words

  • effigiēs pingere — to paint pictures (of what a book describes)

    phrase · also used · classical · Plin. NH 25.8

    Pliny’s words for the Greek herbalists who painted the plants in their books.

  • 1illūstrō: long u (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). From illūstris, of the family of lūx: de Vaan 355, s.v. lūx, illūstris “bright, famous”.

    illūstrō1, illūstrāre, illūstrāvī, illūstrātum — to illustrate (a book)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · modern · M-O s.v. illustration, citing Desfontaines (1798): quī iconibus aut dēscrīptiōnibus rem herbāriam illūstrārunt

    Classically to make clear or famous (see illustrate, make clear); in the botanists the pictures “shed light” on the plants. The sense “put pictures in” follows the modern languages.

Examples

  • pinxēre namque effigiēs herbārum atque ita subscrīpsēre effectūs.

    for they painted pictures of the plants and wrote their properties underneath.Plin. NH 25.8

See also picture, illustrate, book, draw.

SourcesLewis & Short: orno · Lewis & Short: effigies · Lewis & Short: illustro

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. illustration; magazine, periodical, journal.
